text: I loved the moment you called out how tools don’t matter and still seeing real results—that hit home for me because I chased the perfect setup for months. Before this, I was stuck trying to replicate others’ stacks instead of focusing on a repeatable process. I sunk a chunk of time and effort into client work that paid me little return, convinced it was the only path. Then Algorithmic Freedom showed me a different route: separate what I build from what I sell, and own the distribution. I started packaging a simple template pack for teams and the first week it started to move on its own, without me trading hours for cash. The speed of momentum surprised me, and now I’m scaling with fewer hands on deck, which feels liberating.

text: I beg to differ, based on my own personal experience. I’m mid 60’s, semi-retired, former IB like Nate, but more years in that biz. My app knowledge until I started watching Nate’s and a few others videos was using the MS Office suite of products my whole career. I have now build and shipped several unrelated projects that initially started solving a problem I had or a friend had. I knew nothing about how to use Claude Code, I was just using the LLM’s, Anthropic models included, as chat engines for basic questions, research, etc. I think part of what helps someone get over the hump of thinking they can’t do these things is to just get curious and start putting in the reps. I’m now using OpenCode along with very cheap Qwen models for certain builds, and still use Claude Code and Anthropic’s models / mostly Haiku and Sonnet, for more complex work, and to verify what OpenCode builds. 6 months ago I didn’t know what an API was, didn’t know what a Skill and a Repo was, had no idea about any of it. I’m no expert today, but I have now been able to build my own slimmed down version of an AI OS that Nate talks about. There is a ton of opportunity out there, it just requires taking some basic actions, and learning as you go. Most people in Corp America and most SMB’s still don’t really have a great grasp on how to most efficiently use these tools. The two paths Nate mentioned - your own agency route or the corp internal expert - are still wide open. Just get curious, find a problem, and try to solve it. And learn and go from there.
